newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche confident of higher earnings in 97.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche confident of higher earnings in 97.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest commercial bank, said on Wednesday that it expected to post higher profits in 1997 than it did last year.

"We are confident that, if the markets remain favourable, we shall be able to achieve a higher profit for the whole of 1997 than last year," Deutsche management board chairman Rolf Breuer was cited as saying in a press release issued before the bank's interim report news conference.
Breuer also said that cost growth would slow in the second half of the year after rising 26.7 percent in the first half.
Deutsche said the buoyant performance of equity and foreign exchange markets was the main reason for the 27.5 percent rise in group net income to 1.5 billion marks in the first half of 1997.
Operating profit after risk provisions rose 11.4 percent to 2.86 billion marks in the period.

The weakness of the mark had a positive effect on earnings by increasing trading income but it also boosted administration costs which rose 26.7 percent to 8.9 billion marks, Deutsche said in the statement.
Of the cost increase, about seven percentage points came from exchange rate movements of the dollar, the pound and the yen, Deutsche said.
In addition, the effects of the adjustment of pension provisions, which had reduced the cost burden last year, were also felt, Deutsche said.
"The remaining rate of change (in administration costs) of roughly 15 percent is due largely to the further expansion of our infrastructure abroad and the substantial increase in transactions."
The statement quoted chief executive Rolf Breuer as saying: "In the second half our cost management will already produce a lower growth rate than in the first six months."
In the full year 1996 Deutsche posted net income of 2.2 billion marks and operating profit of 5.8 billion marks.
